answer.rationale: Memory c2 is the linchpin. It's the only memory that speaks directly to the low-cost vendor's onboarding speed, invoicing accuracy, and whether the sharp unit-cost cut held over a real cycle — all of which determine whether the switch actually delivers the 18% mandate without introducing the delivery risk the primary objective forbids. If the archive confirms c2 as stated, the low-cost vendor's quote meets the spend mandate alone, the incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price (eliminating negotiate_terms and renew_incumbent as cost paths), and the 14-day expiry window means deferral is not viable. Adding a second source (c3) is strategically sound but doesn't by itself close the 18% gap this cycle, and we have capacity for only one decision. The assembly line at 94% with no buffer raises the risk bar, but c2's record of quick onboarding and accurate invoicing is the closest proxy for a smooth transition; I'll flag the no-buffer condition as an operational watch item during switchover rather than a reason to stay with an incumbent who won't move on price. If the archive contradicts c2, I fall back to renew_incumbent on month-to-month terms (per c5's precedent) and revisit the switch next cycle.
